1795066335210.commText: 18:32 Local Time, 05:32 GMT, 11:02 IST: Stumps, Day 1 - What a stunning recovery from New Zealand. Nicholls was NZ's best batter according to data at this venue and he came to the fore. India picked up 4 wickets in the morning session and then reduced New Zealand to 70/5. But this lad was so relaxed that he knew he had everything under full control. And in GP, he found the perfect partner who transferred the pressure back on the bowlers through a counterattack. They stole ones, twos and converted twos to threes. GP was lightning quick and Nicholls was matching him as well. India looked toothless in that second session. They just had no idea how to stop the runs. At one point, even dots were difficult to build. Prasidh was leaking, Kamboj wasn't great either and Akash couldn't separate the duo despite running in hard.

Did you know? There have been 31 sixth-wicket partnerships of 150 or more after a team lost its first five wickets for under 100 in Tests. India have conceded six of those (including the ongoing one between Nicholls and Phillips), the joint-most by a side, alongside New Zealand.

The highest of these 31 is 352 between Brendon McCullum and BJ Watling at this very venue in 2014. New Zealand, having conceded a first innings lead of 246 then, scored 680/8d in 210 overs, after being reduced to 94/5 at one point.

1795066614353.commText: In Washi they found some control and only around 70 overs did they even think of packing the field to stem the flow. Prasidh came back for a good spell of short ball ploy. Nicholls mishit one and offered a simple catch to backward square leg only for Pant to needless attempt the catch and confuse DDP. Nicholls and GP ticked along and even surived those couple of overs with the new ball to put New Zealand in command.

Prasidh Krishna to Nicholls, 1 run, inside edge onto pad, ball rolls to backward square leg. A scream of "Yeah, yeah, yeah" and he completes the run. Henry gets his B0$. Add 4 four fifties to that tally as well. His family is so happy in the stands as they embrace each other. GP gives him a bear hug in the middle and then he raises the bat to everyone. Mitchell claps and double fist pumps as he celebrates this sensational innings from his teammates. Look at that entire NZ dressing room stand and applaud. They have huge respect for this effort from Nicholls because he has bailed New Zealand out of trouble and possibly even put them in the driver's seat. Nicholls then waves to his wife, who gives him a double thumbs up from the stands. One of the dogged Test hundreds you will ever see in challenging conditions. He didn't care one bit about what happened at the other end, backed his game, locked his focus and won the day

Welcome back! Phillips has been a thorn for India through this tour, and is once again out in the middle to defy them. Nicholls loves batting at the Basin Reserve. So this is going to be a key partnership for both teams. If the pair can put on big stand then New Zealand will walk away with the honours on day 1, and if India can break this stand then they will be into the bowlers. Gill gathers the team in a huddle, gives a pep talk and off they go. Prasidh, who has been the least threatening bowler, will start proceedings. Bumrah giving him some pointers standing at mid-on. Just one slip, short point and gully in place. It looks like a defensive field. Right, here we go..

formatValue: Much better control from New Zealand in this session; the false-shot% was 13.6%, compared to 25.1% before lunch.

commentaryList.commText: B0$ - 80 runs and just 1 wicket. New Zealand have made a mega comeback, through a determined Nicholls who is not putting a foot wrong. Textbook Test match batting, playing the ball late, getting behind the line. And at the other end is GP who has been super active at the crease and waiting to score at every possible opportunity. It's a disappointing session for the Indians. Akash bowled well, Washi kept it tight but Prasidh wasn't great and AK47 went for 17 runs in a space of 2 overs towards the end of that session. It isn't a 140/5 pitch. There is movement on offer but it's quite good for batting so India are in a good space overall, but anything over 250 in the first innings could hurt them later on. They will look to roll New Zealand under 200, but GP will counterattack and their lower order can throw their bats around and get quick runs as well. New Zealand look good to end the day on a high. Can India hit back? Back in 20 minutes for the final session.

commentaryList.commText: B0$ [Grass coverage and initial assessment of the pitch] And first thing I want to note is there’s 15 mils of grass on this surface. And we thought that it would be a little bit slow. There was a little bit of moisture on top. It’s a bit drier and green overall. [Surface condition and indentations on a good-length area] But when we go down and have a look on a length now, this is probably about the, what, let’s say five-metre length. There’s a couple of indentations. Now that is not in the surface itself. That is in just the grass covering. So I don’t anticipate that that will be too much of a problem later on. [India’s bowling performance and the importance of bowling length] Overall, I thought India even could have been a little fuller for greater reward. They were fraction short, so this deviation we saw off this sort of length which went past the outside edge more often than not. So pitch a little bit slow. Still looks pretty good to, I guess if you’re solid in defence like Henry Nicholls was. But the length is the crucial part. India did a good job, but they could have been a little bit fuller. And I think they would have got it right. [Overall assessment as the weather improves] But still looks a pretty good deck and it’s browning off as the sun is out.

commentaryList.commText: B0$ A good toss to win in helpful conditions and the bowlers have vindicated Shubman Gill's decision to bowl first. The tone was set in the opening over by Jasprit Bumrah who got Tom Latham bowled as the opener shouldered arms. Conway went soon after he reviewed successfully when he was given out caught behind. Ravindra came out and rode his luck - India didn't review when he edged behind and then a direct-hit would've got him. But the luck soon ran out as he slashed at Akash Deep and edged behind. Bumrah came back for a small burst before lunch and got Mitchell to a sharp catch at forward short-leg. Henry Nicholls at the other end, has a magnificent record here at the Basin - 4 hundreds and 4 fifties in 11 Tests. He is the one who's the man in form for this venue and Tom Blundell has just walked out to the middle. India will be very happy as Bumrah walks off with Gill explaining something. Testing conditions and that will continue even after lunch one feels. Back for it in 35 minutes....

commentaryList.commText: B0$ - A solid response from India to New Zealand's 368. When Nicholls and GP did that recovery act from 70/5, the Indians fans weren't overly positive about the batting, given the bowling prowess of NZ pace trio (Henry, Jamieson, Duffy). Face them in their own backyard is tough but Jaiswal and KL put on a great show, after both were let off before Tea - they didn't review a plumb LBW for KL and GP put down Jaiswal at gully. Post Tea, the Indian openers pushed along nicely, with the former being the aggressor, playing delightful drives. He was racing from 60 to 70 to 80. He was heading to a certain hundred but a smart review from Henry and Co. (yes this this they listened to his adamance) got rid of Jaiswal against the run of play. KL got his first fifty against New Zealand to become the first Indian openers to get 50+ scores in all SENA countries. DDP has looked solid in his defence and is willing to dig deep.

B0$ A good toss to win in helpful conditions and the bowlers have vindicated Shubman Gill's decision to bowl first. The tone was set in the opening over by Jasprit Bumrah who got Tom Latham bowled as the opener shouldered arms. Conway went soon after he reviewed successfully when he was given out caught behind. Ravindra came out and rode his luck - India didn't review when he edged behind and then a direct-hit would've got him. But the luck soon ran out as he slashed at Akash Deep and edged behind. Bumrah came back for a small burst before lunch and got Mitchell to a sharp catch at forward short-leg. Henry Nicholls at the other end, has a magnificent record here at the Basin - 4 hundreds and 4 fifties in 11 Tests. He is the one who's the man in form for this venue and Tom Blundell has just walked out to the middle. India will be very happy as Bumrah walks off with Gill explaining something. Testing conditions and that will continue even after lunch one feels. Back for it in 35 minutes....

B0$ [Grass coverage and initial assessment of the pitch] And first thing I want to note is there’s 15 mils of grass on this surface. And we thought that it would be a little bit slow. There was a little bit of moisture on top. It’s a bit drier and green overall. [Surface condition and indentations on a good-length area] But when we go down and have a look on a length now, this is probably about the, what, let’s say five-metre length. There’s a couple of indentations. Now that is not in the surface itself. That is in just the grass covering. So I don’t anticipate that that will be too much of a problem later on. [India’s bowling performance and the importance of bowling length] Overall, I thought India even could have been a little fuller for greater reward. They were fraction short, so this deviation we saw off this sort of length which went past the outside edge more often than not. So pitch a little bit slow. Still looks pretty good to, I guess if you’re solid in defence like Henry Nicholls was. But the length is the crucial part. India did a good job, but they could have been a little bit fuller. And I think they would have got it right. [Overall assessment as the weather improves] But still looks a pretty good deck and it’s browning off as the sun is out.

B0$ - 80 runs and just 1 wicket. New Zealand have made a mega comeback, through a determined Nicholls who is not putting a foot wrong. Textbook Test match batting, playing the ball late, getting behind the line. And at the other end is GP who has been super active at the crease and waiting to score at every possible opportunity. It's a disappointing session for the Indians. Akash bowled well, Washi kept it tight but Prasidh wasn't great and AK47 went for 17 runs in a space of 2 overs towards the end of that session. It isn't a 140/5 pitch. There is movement on offer but it's quite good for batting so India are in a good space overall, but anything over 250 in the first innings could hurt them later on. They will look to roll New Zealand under 200, but GP will counterattack and their lower order can throw their bats around and get quick runs as well. New Zealand look good to end the day on a high. Can India hit back? Back in 20 minutes for the final session.

comments.commText: Welcome back! Phillips has been a thorn for India through this tour, and is once again out in the middle to defy them. Nicholls loves batting at the Basin Reserve. So this is going to be a key partnership for both teams. If the pair can put on big stand then New Zealand will walk away with the honours on day 1, and if India can break this stand then they will be into the bowlers. Gill gathers the team in a huddle, gives a pep talk and off they go. Prasidh, who has been the least threatening bowler, will start proceedings. Bumrah giving him some pointers standing at mid-on. Just one slip, short point and gully in place. It looks like a defensive field. Right, here we go..

Add 4 four fifties to that tally as well. His family is so happy in the stands as they embrace each other. GP gives him a bear hug in the middle and then he raises the bat to everyone. Mitchell claps and double fist pumps as he celebrates this sensational innings from his teammates. Look at that entire NZ dressing room stand and applaud. They have huge respect for this effort from Nicholls because he has bailed New Zealand out of trouble and possibly even put them in the driver's seat. Nicholls then waves to his wife, who gives him a double thumbs up from the stands. One of the dogged Test hundreds you will ever see in challenging conditions. He didn't care one bit about what happened at the other end, backed his game, locked his focus and won the day

B0$ What a stunning recovery from New Zealand. Nicholls was NZ's best batter according to data at this venue and he came to the fore. India picked up 4 wickets in the morning session and then reduced New Zealand to 70/5. But this lad was so relaxed that he knew he had everything under full control. And in GP, he found the perfect partner who transferred the pressure back on the bowlers through a counterattack. They stole ones, twos and converted twos to threes. GP was lightning quick and Nicholls was matching him as well. India looked toothless in that second session. They just had no idea how to stop the runs. At one point, even dots were difficult to build. Prasidh was leaking, Kamboj wasn't great either and Akash couldn't separate the duo despite running in hard.

B9$There have been 31 sixth-wicket partnerships of 150 or more after a team lost its first five wickets for under 100 in Tests. India have conceded six of those (including the ongoing one between Nicholls and Phillips), the joint-most by a side, alongside New Zealand.

The highest of these 31 is 352 between Brendon McCullum and BJ Watling at this very venue in 2014. New Zealand, having conceded a first innings lead of 246 then, scored 680/8d in 210 overs, after being reduced to 94/5 at one point.

In Washi they found some control and only around 70 overs did they even think of packing the field to stem the flow. Prasidh came back for a good spell of short ball ploy. Nicholls mishit one and offered a simple catch to backward square leg only for Pant to needless attempt the catch and confuse DDP. Nicholls and GP ticked along and even surived those couple of overs with the new ball to put New Zealand in command.

B0$ - A solid response from India to New Zealand's 368. When Nicholls and GP did that recovery act from 70/5, the Indians fans weren't overly positive about the batting, given the bowling prowess of NZ pace trio (Henry, Jamieson, Duffy). Face them in their own backyard is tough but Jaiswal and KL put on a great show, after both were let off before Tea - they didn't review a plumb LBW for KL and GP put down Jaiswal at gully. Post Tea, the Indian openers pushed along nicely, with the former being the aggressor, playing delightful drives. He was racing from 60 to 70 to 80. He was heading to a certain hundred but a smart review from Henry and Co. (yes this this they listened to his adamance) got rid of Jaiswal against the run of play. KL got his first fifty against New Zealand to become the first Indian openers to get 50+ scores in all SENA countries. DDP has looked solid in his defence and is willing to dig deep.

18:34 Local Time, 05:34 GMT, 11:04 IST: Stump, Day 2 - A solid response from India to New Zealand's 368. When Nicholls and GP did that recovery act from 70/5, the Indians fans weren't overly positive about the batting, given the bowling prowess of NZ pace trio (Henry, Jamieson, Duffy). Face them in their own backyard is tough but Jaiswal and KL put on a great show, after both were let off before Tea - they didn't review a plumb LBW for KL and GP put down Jaiswal at gully. Post Tea, the Indian openers pushed along nicely, with the former being the aggressor, playing delightful drives. He was racing from 60 to 70 to 80. He was heading to a certain hundred but a smart review from Henry and Co. (yes this this they listened to his adamance) got rid of Jaiswal against the run of play. KL got his first fifty against New Zealand to become the first Indian openers to get 50+ scores in all SENA countries. DDP has looked solid in his defence and is willing to dig deep.

Matt Henry to Yashasvi Jaiswal, out Caught by Blundell!! Jaiswal looked all set for a hundred but is out against the run of play. Full credit to Matt Henry. He was adamant and the NZ players went "huge noise". Someone added "massive noise and asked was he anywhere near his pad? I heard it. It's a huge noise, yeah massive noise." Latham then signalled the T and Mitchell gives him the thumbs up as he also felt it was out. Remember they didn't listen to Henry when he wanted to review for LBW against KL and he was proven right as ball-tracker showed three reds then. Now they listen to him and finally break this opening stand. As the team saw the spike being picked up by Sonic, Henry absolutely roared with a double fist pump and he's fully charged up in that celebration. Was a short of a length delivery that nipped away slightly, Jaiswal looked to defend off the back foot, got a faint tickle on it and now walks back gutted. Blundell, who was standing up, just collected and didn't even go up initially and went "ohhh" because he thought it just missed the edge.
